new_findings_today.title: Intermittent React #418 hydration exception on editorial surfaces (/en landing, /en/explore) — ~50% of loads, never on destination pages
new_findings_today.detail: Minified React error #418 (hydration mismatch, args[]=HTML) thrown from the main app chunk during hydration. 4 controlled observations: /en/explore first navigate → FIRED; /en/explore F5 reload → clean; /en F5 reload → FIRED; /en fresh navigate (cache-busting query) → clean. 0 errors on any of the 5 destination pages probed (kodaikanal, vagator, jaipur, betla, vishnuprayag). Pages recover visually (React falls back to client render) — no user-visible breakage observed, but hydration fallback costs client CPU on the two highest-traffic surfaces and signals server/client HTML divergence. Both affected surfaces are the editorial template; suspects include time/issue-sensitive masthead content (ISSUE N° 48 · JUNE 2026), the rotating landing hero (h1 was 'Alchi.' on one load), or month-aware copy ('Showing scores for June').
new_findings_today.evidence: Console captures in session: identical stack via rX/iu/sd in chunk 13w0ldxt56tn..js?dpl=dpl_CNZXAShTjajrtqTxZbhGM9FNXSaj at 02:18:03Z (explore), 02:21:23Z (/en post-F5); clean reads at 02:18:29Z (explore reload) and 02:22Z (/en fresh). section-K-map.csv rows explore-grid + landing-/en.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Run /en locally with non-minified React to get the full mismatch diff. Audit the editorial template for Date.now()/locale-dependent or randomized SSR output (rotating hero pick is the classic culprit — pin the choice server-side and pass it as a prop). Honest caveat: yesterday's pass recorded 0 console errors on explore, but its console attach timing may not have captured load-time exceptions, so 'new today' vs 'newly observed' is not certain.

business_summary.headline: GREEN. Everything customer-facing passed: all 21 core routes, all 10 sampled destination pages in both English and Hindi, every SEO check, the API layer, PWA assets, and the 26k-URL sitemap. Emergency SOS is in its strongest verified state — every one of 525 destinations has real, dialable emergency numbers in the database (zero placeholders site-wide), and every sampled page renders them. Best news of the day: the explore map's 'missing markers' scare is conclusively dead — all 511 score-colored markers render and were visually confirmed; the probe had been looking in the wrong place for a month. One new watch item: an intermittent, self-recovering React warning on the landing and explore pages that users don't see but that deserves a developer look.

bottom_line: Ask the developer to spend 30 minutes on the React #418 warning with a non-minified build — prime suspect is the rotating hero/issue masthead rendering differently on server vs client.
Fix the static atlas coordinates (one template variable) — small effort, visible credibility win.
Schedule the overdue deep accessibility + Lighthouse pass once the Leaflet destination-map rollout finishes, so it's measured once, not twice.
